title: Aramco Ventures Leads $9.5 Million Round in India's Mitti Labs to Cut Methane From Rice Farming
excerpt: The New York- and Bengaluru-based climate-tech startup plans to expand across Southeast Asia while scaling its carbon credits and agricultural data business.
body:
• India-focused climate-tech startup Mitti Labs has raised $9.5 million in a Series A round led by Aramco Ventures, Saudi Aramco's venture capital arm.
  • The company works with over 70,000 smallholder farmers across six Indian states, using AI-powered satellite monitoring to cut methane emissions from rice farming by up to 50% and water use by up to 40%.
  • Mitti Labs plans to expand beyond India into the Philippines and Indonesia, targeting rice-growing regions most vulnerable to water stress.
  • Rice farming accounts for roughly 12% of global methane emissions — a figure comparable to global aviation — making it a high-impact target for climate intervention.

Mitti Labs, a climate-tech startup headquartered in New York and Bengaluru, has raised $9.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Aramco Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco, according to TechCrunch. The investment will fund the company's expansion across Southeast Asia as it scales its carbon credits business and agricultural data platform.

Founded in 2023 by Harvard Business School graduates Xavier Laguarta and Devdut Dalal, along with CTO Nathan Torbick, Mitti Labs has carved out a niche in one of agriculture's most stubborn climate problems: the methane emissions generated by flooded rice paddies. Rice farming produces roughly 12% of global methane output — a volume on par with global aviation — while consuming approximately 30% of the world's freshwater supply.

How It Works

The startup helps farmers adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying, or AWD, an irrigation technique that periodically allows rice fields to dry instead of keeping them continuously flooded. The method can reduce water use by up to 40% and methane emissions by up to 50% without compromising yields, according to the company.

To verify these reductions, Mitti Labs deploys a digital Measurement, Reporting, and Verification platform that combines high-resolution satellite imagery from synthetic aperture radars with on-ground gas chamber data. The system uses AI models trained on this combined data to accurately measure climate impact — a critical capability for generating high-integrity carbon credits that buyers in Europe and the United States will pay for.

The company has partnered with organizations including The Nature Conservancy, the Syngenta Foundation, Dr. Reddy's Foundation, and Spanish food processor Ebro Foods. Its PRANA program with The Nature Conservancy in Punjab is projected to save 500 billion liters of water — roughly equivalent to the annual consumption of a mid-sized city.

Scaling Across Asia

With the new funding, Mitti Labs plans to expand beyond India into the Philippines and Indonesia — two of Asia's largest rice producers, where water stress is intensifying due to climate change. Rice farming occupies 150 million hectares across Asia, an area roughly three times the size of California.

The company currently works with more than 70,000 smallholder farmers across six Indian states, up from 40,000 at the time of its $3 million seed round in mid-2024. It has launched projects covering tens of thousands of hectares and plans to mitigate hundreds of thousands of tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions annually.

"If you're trying to do five different things, that's a good strategy for some people. For us, the importance is we want to be the best in rice farming."

— Xavier Laguarta, Co-founder, Mitti Labs

The Carbon Credits Angle

Mitti Labs' business model centers on monetizing verified methane reductions through carbon credits, with at least 70% of profits distributed to participating farmers as additional income — potentially boosting their annual earnings by up to 30%. The company works with Gold Standard for carbon credit certification and recently partnered with Cool Effect, a U.S.-based carbon credit platform focused on methane reduction.

The involvement of Aramco Ventures is notable. Saudi Arabia's state oil company has invested $1.5 billion in sustainability-focused ventures as part of its net-zero 2050 ambitions. The investment in Mitti Labs aligns with Aramco's broader strategy of backing carbon reduction technologies across the agricultural and industrial sectors.

Why It Matters for India

India is the world's second-largest rice producer, and millions of its farmers depend on rice cultivation for their livelihoods. Climate change has driven a significant decline in water levels across major rice-growing regions, while methane from paddy fields contributes substantially to India's greenhouse gas emissions.

For the Indian diaspora, the investment signals growing international confidence in India's climate-tech ecosystem. The startup's model — using technology to lift farmer incomes while cutting emissions — represents the kind of scalable solution that India's agricultural sector urgently needs as it confronts the dual pressures of food security and climate adaptation.
